problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the annual budget across 13 infrastructure projects to maximize the total community benefit score.  
The characteristics of each project are:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.070, impact factor 0.244, allocation limits [0.006, 0.878]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.052, impact factor 0.061, allocation limits [0.081, 0.419]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.044, impact factor 0.155, allocation limits [0.048, 0.646]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.124, impact factor 0.299, allocation limits [0.063, 0.689]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.061, impact factor 0.256, allocation limits [0.045, 0.405]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.038, impact factor 0.160, allocation limits [0.033, 0.768]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.069, impact factor 0.219, allocation limits [0.036, 0.513]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.062, impact factor 0.238, allocation limits [0.056, 0.704]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.098, impact factor 0.097, allocation limits [0.093, 0.592]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.089, impact factor 0.173, allocation limits [0.026, 0.742]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.046, impact factor 0.175, allocation limits [0.002, 0.834]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.193, impact factor 0.126, allocation limits [0.012, 0.529]  
* Project M: benefit score 0.047, impact factor 0.210, allocation limits [0.087, 0.472]  

Each project must receive a budget share within its specified limits, and the total allocation across all projects must sum to one. To ensure equitable regional development, the subset of projects in high-priority zones, denoted P = {E, G, H, J, K}, must collectively receive at least 0.512 of the total budget. Additionally, the overall community impact index must not exceed 0.272, and the total benefit score must be at least 0.066. Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
